data.title: Bitcoin (BTC) Has Hit Bottom, Says JPMorgan Chase
data.description:
JPMorgan Chase (JPM) has called a bottom in Bitcoin (BTC) after the largest cryptocurrency declined 20% over the past month. JPMorgan's chief cryptocurrency analyst, Nikolaos Panigirtzoglou, said that Bitcoin has likely reached "capitulation" after nearly two months of selling.

In a note to clients, Panigirtzoglou highlighted the record outflows from Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) during November, which are on track to top $5 billion, as a sign of a potential bottom. "The speed of the outflows has, if anything, been more intense than the outflows from early May to late June this year," he wrote.

The JPMorgan analyst added that retail investors likely drove much of the recent crypto ETF outflows and may have sold to buy stocks such as the newly public Anthropic (ANT).

The Strategy Factor

In addition to the ETF outflows, Panigirtzoglou cited an unconventional method to call a likely bottom in Bitcoin, with its price hovering near $60,000. The analyst cited a drop in Strategy's (MSTR) valuation relative to its Bitcoin holdings to a record low as a sign that capitulation has likely been reached.

Panigirtzoglou wrote that the ratio has fallen to around 0.88x, below the previous low seen in June of this year. The analysts' charts compare Strategy's enterprise value with the dollar value of its Bitcoin holdings, though the report does not specify the exact formula used.

Strategy's NAV Calculation

Strategy has its own way of calculating the ratio, which it calls mNAV. The company divides its common share price by the dollar value of its Bitcoin holdings per share. "The premium to NAV collapses to a new record low of 0.88 for MicroStrategy's stock, signaling capitulation in Bitcoin," wrote the analyst.

Bitcoin's price has fallen back to around $60,000 after recovering briefly from last week's two-year low of $56,000. Bitcoin was is rising in early trading on Nov. 27 and on track to end a seven-week losing streak that is its second-longest decline on record.

BTC Price Action

Below is a chart from TipRanks that looks at the price movements of Bitcoin over the past three months. As one can see, the price of BTC is down 24% in the last 12 weeks.

data.title: NetApp (NTAP) Reports Q2 Earnings on December 2 — Here's What Analysts Expect
data.description:
U.S. enterprise storage vendor NetApp (NTAP) is preparing to release its fiscal Q2 2027 earnings next Tuesday, December 1, after the market closes. NTAP stock is up about 54% since the start of the year. Still, analysts are split over whether the company can sustain its growth.

For reference, Wall Street expects NetApp to report revenue of $2.11 billion, up by 24% from $1.70 billion last year. Adjusted earnings per share are forecast to rise 27% to $2.61, up from $2.05 in the year-ago quarter.

Goldman Sachs Is Bullish on Higher Selling Price

Recently, Goldman Sachs analyst Katherine Murphy maintained her Buy rating on NetApp shares. She also kept her price target at $240, predicting about 42% upside.

According to Murphy, two major debates surround NetApp heading into earnings. One is whether demand for AI storage products will last rather than be a short-lived boom.

The other is whether rising component costs will hurt the company's product gross margins. Cautious investors believe that rising costs and wider adoption of long-term agreements that lock in deals at today's prices could hurt profit levels.

However, Murphy raised her estimates for NetApp's fiscal 2027 and 2028 sales and EPS. She believes the company can make more money through higher average selling prices. This is because she sees the firm as able to pass on most of its rising input costs to customers.

Why Oppenheimer Is Staying on the Sidelines

By contrast, Oppenheimer analyst Param Singh recently maintained his Hold rating on NetApp shares. He did not set a new price target. The analyst expects NetApp to beat its own revenue forecast for the quarter.

Singh's checks with NetApp's industry clients suggested that the company will beat earnings expectations for the quarter. The analyst found that clients expect spending on core data-storage systems to keep rising.

The checks also suggested that customers see NetApp performing better than peers. However, Singh remains cautious, preferring to see whether current growth is temporary or sustainable. He suspects price increases and customers pulling purchases forward are driving growth.

"The upcoming quarter should help establish whether spending strength and competitive gains can sustain growth beyond pricing benefits and accelerated purchases," Singh noted.

Is NetApp a Good Stock to Buy?

On Wall Street, analysts rate NetApp's shares a Moderate Buy, by consensus, according to TipRanks' data. This reflects six Buys and 12 Holds assigned over the past three months.

However, the average NTAP price target of $210.20 implies about 24% upside (see NTAP stock forecast here).

data.title: Why Is Alibaba (BABA) Stock Up 4% Today, 11/27/26?
data.description:
Alibaba (BABA) is up by over 4% on Friday as Chinese stocks stage a rally following new measures from Beijing aimed at supporting the country's stock market. In a State Council meeting, Chinese Premier Li Qiang urged a greater role by state-backed investors, also known as the "National Team," in supporting the stock market.

The Chinese government called on Central Huijin, a major state-backed investment fund, to strengthen its role as a market stabilizer and provide liquidity during periods of volatility. Beijing also plans to encourage publicly traded companies to increase dividends and share buybacks.

BABA Stock Rallies as Beijing Moves to Support Chinese Stocks

The announcement drove a sharp rally across Chinese markets. The Shanghai Composite gained more than 3%, while the CSI 300 jumped over 4%. Meanwhile, the tech-heavy STAR 50 Index surged around 15%, reflecting a rebound in beaten-down technology and semiconductor stocks.

Alibaba is rising alongside other Chinese stocks as investors welcome Beijing's latest policies. BABA stock has faced pressure in recent months amid concerns about China's economy and weakness in AI stocks. The new measures are helping improve investor sentiment, although they don't directly change Alibaba's business outlook.

The measures are intended to attract more long-term institutional capital into China's stock market and reduce selling pressure during periods of volatility. For Alibaba, a recovery in Chinese equities could help support its share price after months of weakness. Still, the policy announcements do not address the company-specific challenges facing its e-commerce and cloud businesses.

Furthermore, investors will want to see Beijing follow through on its promises. The government has yet to specify how much money state-backed funds will invest or when the new measures will take effect.

Should You Buy BABA Stock?

Wall Street believes that BABA stock should be priced significantly higher. During the past three months, analysts have issued an average BABA price target of $172.13, implying upside of 99.55% from current prices. The highest price target sits at $207, while the lowest is at $128. Of the 16 analysts covering BABA, 16 rate it a Buy, zero rate it a Hold, and none rate it a Sell.

data.title: Anthropic vs. Coinbase: One Stock Is Overhyped, One Is Oversold, Says Top Investor
data.description:
Crypto bulls spent the fall waiting for fresh money to find its way back to them. Some of it may have gone to the year's most anticipated listing instead. Days before Anthropic (NASDAQ:ANT) made its Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19, an executive at Coinbase (NASDAQ:COIN) called the idea that AI IPOs are drawing risk capital away from bitcoin "a reasonable argument."

Neither stock has had much to cheer about since. Anthropic closed below its $83 IPO price in the two sessions before Thanksgiving, then climbed above it ahead of Friday's shortened session. Coinbase is also rising today, but sits near a three-year low, even as bitcoin heads for its first weekly gain in two months.

5-star investor Dilantha De Silva went through the numbers on both companies, and they led him to different places.

With Anthropic, De Silva starts with margins. The company counts only the cost of running its models for customers against revenue, while the cost of training new models goes under research and development. On that basis, its gross margin is about 85%. The investor isn't convinced. Models released in the six months to Sept. 30 generated more than 80% of third-quarter revenue, which suggests each one earns most of its money for only a short time before it's replaced. To him, that makes training an ongoing cost of doing business rather than a long-term investment. Counting all compute and infrastructure spending, roughly 57% of revenue in the first nine months, he puts the gross margin closer to 43%.

He has a similar issue with sales made through the cloud marketplaces run by Amazon, Google and Microsoft, which handled about 44% of revenue over those nine months. When a customer buys Claude this way, Anthropic counts the full price as revenue, even though the cloud provider keeps a cut. Those fees go under sales, marketing and partnerships instead, an expense line that grew to about 17% of revenue from around 13% a year earlier. In the investor's view, that makes Anthropic's revenue look larger than what it actually keeps.

Revenue per dollar of compute comes next. De Silva gives the company credit for the steep rise since early 2025, but the figure fell to 1.72x in Q3 from just over 2x in Q2. Compute costs climbed about 77% from the previous quarter while revenue rose 47%, partly because Anthropic spent $5 billion on costly short-term capacity. With about $71 billion in commitments due over the next 12 months, he expects more pressure.

Then there's competition. With products like Claude Docs, Sheets and Meetings, Anthropic is now selling tools that compete with Microsoft's and Google's own office software, even though those two companies also sell a large share of Anthropic's products through their cloud marketplaces. De Silva sees this expansion into business software as Anthropic's best chance for growth, but it also risks upsetting the partners it depends on.

He doesn't expect Anthropic to stumble, yet with a market cap of about $1.1 trillion, he thinks the stock leaves little room for error.

Bottom line, De Silva rates ANT a Hold. (To watch De Silva's track record, click here)

Turning to Coinbase, subscription and services made up 49% of net revenue in Q3. That's welcome, the investor says, but probably not enough to move the shares on its own. So he turns to the balance sheet. Coinbase ended September with $8.6 billion in cash and cash equivalents against $6 billion of long-term debt. None of that debt comes due before 2028, after the company paid off $1.3 billion of convertible notes in June. In his view, that rules out near-term solvency worries, even before counting the company's crypto holdings.

The cash also funds buybacks. Coinbase repurchased about 7.1 million shares for roughly $1.25 billion in the first nine months and has close to $2 billion of authorization left.

De Silva isn't trying to time a bitcoin recovery, though he admits the stock still tends to move with it. He doesn't own any crypto himself, and Coinbase gives him that exposure through the coins it holds on its own books. If bitcoin rallied 50%, he estimates the company's pre-tax income would get a boost of about $1.1 billion from those holdings alone.

His case doesn't depend on that happening, though. His base case has bitcoin trading between $65,000 and $80,000 through 2027. In that scenario, spot trading revenue drops about 16% year over year, but derivatives and prediction markets, which have passed $200 million in annualized revenue, make up the difference. He estimates adjusted EBITDA would rise about 28% YoY, with the margin reaching about 30%.

De Silva does point to some risks. Lower rates could reduce stablecoin income, the USDC business leans on a single partner, and a severe crypto crash would be hard to model. Even so, the investor believes Coinbase can grow earnings without a bitcoin rally, and that the market will eventually treat it as part of crypto's plumbing rather than a stand-in for bitcoin.

All told, he rates COIN a Buy.

On the Street, ANT claims a Strong Buy consensus rating, its $150.50 average price target implying shares will gain 82% over the coming months. COIN is rated a Moderate Buy. At $192.52, its average target points to 12-month returns of 86%. (See ANT stock forecast or COIN stock forecast)

data.title: IREN Stock Jumps in Pre-Market, but Technical Signals Still Flash 'Sell'
data.description:
Shares of Australian data center developer IREN Limited (IREN) jumped 8% to about $14 during Friday's pre-market trading. Despite a 23.86% rally on Monday, November 23, the shares are down about 12% this week. On Wall Street, analysts rate IREN stock a Moderate Buy, according to TipRanks' data. However, TipRanks' IREN Technical Analysis tool still flags a "Sell" overall consensus based on a one-week time frame.

Why IREN Shares Came Under Pressure This Week

IREN shares rallied 23.86% on Monday, November 23, after Jensen Huang was reinstated as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO. This eased fears that the American chipmaker might cut back on support for the neocloud industry.

However, shares in the Sydney-based company plunged 11.54% to $12.95 the following day. This came as fears of a possible slowdown in AI spending returned.

What IREN Stock Technical Signals Show

TipRanks' Technical Analysis tool for IREN shares currently reflects an overall "Sell" consensus. This is based on 14 bearish, three Neutral, and five Bullish signals recorded over the past week.

Breaking it down, the technical analysis consensus shows Buy. However, the moving average consensus is a "Strong Sell," as shown in the image above.

In addition, the 20- and 50-Day moving averages both indicate Sell. These are based on IREN's average price over roughly the past one-month and 2.5-month periods, respectively.

On a brighter note, while the one-week Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) indicator is at -7.86, it still suggests that IREN is a Buy. The indicator compares short- and longer-term price movements. A Buy rating from this indicator suggests the signal detects a potential rebound.

Here's Where Analysts Stand on IREN Stock

IREN shares currently boast Buy ratings from several analysts. However, some analysts have chosen to stay cautious with Hold ratings.

For instance, Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei recently called IREN stock a Buy. Rezaei weighed in on IREN shifting its annual recurring revenue target timeline from year-end to January 2027. She argued that IREN's actual computing capacity remains contracted and funded.

By contrast, Goldman Sachs analyst Michael Ng is worried about a higher risk of deployment delays in the industry. He also believes that high borrowing costs remain a concern for neocloud companies. As a result, Ng recently maintained his Hold rating on the company.

Is IREN a Good Stock to Buy Now?

data.title: Palantir Stock (PLTR) Has No Room for Error at This Valuation
data.description:
Palantir Technologies, Inc. (PLTR) stock has little room for error at its current valuation, despite the company's strong growth. The Florida-based software platform developer has lost 8% of its market value so far this year, even after delivering standout Q3 results and raising full-year guidance across key financial metrics. Yet following that pullback, shares still trade at a steep forward P/E multiple of 96x.

Although Palantir's rapid top-line expansion justifies a premium valuation, a closer look at total contract value (TCV), the international commercial segment, and the earnings sensitivity to certain macro developments suggests the stock is already priced for perfection. For these reasons, I am Bearish on Palantir.

Slow TCV Growth Raises Questions

One of the main reasons behind my Bearish stance on Palantir is the massive gap between TCV growth and revenue growth. In Q3 2026, TCV grew just 6% year-over-year to $2.92 billion, while revenue surged 96% year-over-year to $2.31 billion. Meanwhile, year-over-year TCV growth decelerated sharply from 49% in Q2 when TCV reached $3.37 billion.

At a fundamental level, the disconnect between revenue growth and TCV growth highlights shorter initial contract durations for new contracts. This contrasts with Palantir's historical operational profile, when the company enjoyed multi-year government contracts. On the Q3 earnings call, CFO David Glazer revealed that several eight-figure contracts were shorter in duration compared to historical averages.

CFO Glazer elaborated that he expects contract durations to eventually increase. "We signed multiple 8-figure deals in the quarter that were shorter in duration than usual, as customers rapidly adopted initial sovereign AI capabilities in their enterprise. It is important to remember that the sovereign AI revolution is only 1 quarter old. As we continue to deliver value with sovereign AI, over time, we expect both the duration and size of these contracts to increase."

From a valuation perspective, the problem with shorter contract durations is that customers reach renewal or renegotiation dates sooner. Strong revenue conversion today does not automatically lock in multi-year cash flows unless Palantir sustains high retention and expands initial terms at renewal. Slow TCV growth, therefore, highlights this risk faced by the company. I believe Palantir's valuation multiples will continue to compress in the next few quarters as the market digests this business transition.

International Commercial Segment Is a Slow Compounder

My Bearish stance on Palantir is strengthened by the slower growth seen in international commercial business. In Q3, international commercial revenue grew 21% year-over-year to $184 million. Sequentially, this represented just 1% growth. In comparison, the U.S. commercial business reported 148% year-over-year revenue growth to $984 million in Q3. From a longer-term perspective, the massive gap between U.S. and international growth within the commercial business raises questions about global adoption of Palantir's products.

Certain macro indicators suggest the global IT spending environment is not supportive of Palantir's growth. For instance, according to Gartner (IT), European IT spending is expected to reach $1.57 trillion in 2027, with data center systems spending and infrastructure spending expected to emerge as growth hotspots. This indicates global IT budgets are shifting toward compute and infrastructure, which is bad news for application-layer companies such as Palantir.

The regulatory environment in international markets is complicated as well. This presents a challenge for Palantir. In the European Union (EU), companies are expected to comply with the EU Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act, the Cyber Resilience Act, the EU Data Act, and the revised Product Liability Directive. Longer legal reviews, vendor compliance questionnaires, and governance audits slow down pilot-to-production conversion in Europe compared to the United States. Palantir's adoption, therefore, will be slow and gradual.

U.S. Commercial Growth Mainly Comes from Existing Accounts

Another factor that has contributed to my Bearish stance on Palantir is the customer concentration within its U.S. commercial business. In Q3, Palantir grew U.S. commercial customer count by 29% year-over-year to 686, up just 5% sequentially. This segment's strong revenue growth was driven by an 88% year-over-year increase in trailing-12-month (TTM) revenue per U.S. commercial customer.

Net dollar retention reached 165% as well. These data points suggest that Palantir's U.S. commercial growth relies heavily on expanding existing accounts and closing large deals rather than broadening the customer base. If net dollar retention cools from 165% or large account expansions slow, top-line growth will decelerate sharply.

Palantir Is Valued for Perfection

At a forward P/E multiple of 96x, I believe Palantir is valued for flawless execution. That valuation represents a steep premium of more than five times the sector median of 18.2x and well ahead of enterprise software peers such as Datadog (DDOG) at 57.79x and ServiceNow (NOW) at 23.3x.

This is where I believe investing in Palantir exposes investors to a meaningful downside risk. Paying that kind of multiple assumes shorter deal durations and slower bookings growth will not weigh on future revenue recognition. This, however, is a risky assumption that could backfire if revenue growth slows as TCV growth slows. At the same time, international commercial adoption remains a slower growth engine.

I am also wary of the valuation implications of Palantir's revenue growth relying heavily on existing-account expansion. If net retention moderates, international traction stays muted, or revenue growth decelerates, Palantir's earnings multiples will compress sharply.

Is Palantir a Buy, According to Wall Street Analysts?

On TipRanks, based on ratings from 25 Wall Street analysts, the average Palantir price target is $229.09, implying 40% upside from the current market price.

Takeaway

Palantir's stock market performance has been lackluster in 2026. Although the company has continued to grow at a strong pace, its valuation seems to have run ahead of the economic reality it has faced over the past few years. This has led to a valuation multiple compression this year. Looking ahead, I believe there are a few factors that could continue to exert pressure on Palantir's valuation multiples. For this reason, I am Bearish on Palantir's prospects.

data.title: Anthropic Shares Rebound Past $83 IPO Price While $140 Billion Co-Founder Stake Stays Locked Until May 2027
data.description:
Anthropic shares (ANT) climbed back past their $83 IPO price in a Friday premarket rebound to $86.01. Even so, a $140 billion co-founder stake stays locked off the market until May 2027. ANT stock had already snapped a three-day slide on Wednesday with a 1.08% gain to $82.79.

Even after that bounce, the Claude developer trades below its $97.17 debut close from Nov. 19. Worries over cloud-provider debt and data-center spending dragged the shares down 15% earlier this week, while stubborn U.S. inflation lifted bets on more Federal Reserve rate hikes.

Anthropic's Nov. 18 listing raised $93.5 billion in public stock plus $26 billion in private placements from backers such as Nvidia (NVDA) and Alphabet (GOOGL). At $83 a share, the deal valued the business at $1.49 trillion on a fully diluted basis, or 18 times its $81 billion October annualized revenue run rate. Its SEC Form 424(b)(4) prospectus also lists $900.9 billion in long-term compute commitments, with $70.7 billion due within 12 months.

Anthropic's Co-Founders Hold 1.69 Billion Restricted Shares Until Spring 2027

Public trading covers roughly 6% of Anthropic's fully diluted stock, while 15.5 billion pre-IPO shares sit under lockups across 23 release dates. CEO Dario Amodei and President Daniela Amodei joined the five other co-founders in selling 3,378,378 shares each at $83 during the offering, SEC Form 4 filings show. That $1.96 billion combined sale cashed out just 1.4% of their holdings.

All seven co-founders still hold roughly 1.69 billion Anthropic shares and equity awards, equal to 12.7% of shares outstanding. The Bloomberg Billionaires Index valued those $ANT stakes near $140 billion at the $83 offer price. Select pre-IPO Anthropic stockholders can sell up to 303 million shares starting Dec. 15, yet the co-founders cannot sell any stock this winter.

Anthropic's co-founders get their first selling window two trading days after first-quarter 2027 earnings or on May 17, 2027, whichever comes first. Up to 29% of their locked ANT stake unlocks then, equal to about 490 million shares worth $40.6 billion at Wednesday's close.

The remaining 71% of Anthropic's founder equity, or 1.20 billion shares worth $99.3 billion, stays restricted until after third-quarter 2027 results or Nov. 18, 2027. One Class F share keeps 50.1% voting power with the co-founders, whose pledge to donate 80% of their personal Anthropic stock is "revocable and not legally binding" under the prospectus.

Is Anthropic Stock a Good Buy?

On TipRanks, ANT has a Strong Buy consensus rating based on 10 Buys and one Hold rating. The average 12-month Anthropic price target of $150.50 implies 81.8% upside potential from current levels. (See ANT stock forecast)
